text:
anya: Heads-up — bringing up BN-Embed-v2 on the staging holdout set, seeing a strange cluster collapse compared to bn-embed-v1. recall@10 down ~6%. anyone free?
liam: i'm free quick. what does the run id look like and which quant config?
anya: run id run_2026_03_21_bn_v2. quant=fp16->int8 per-channel, clamp=0.98. batchnorm folded into linear as discussed.
nina: that clamp value seems tight. did you run the on-the-fly whitening step?
anya: yes, whitening applied same as baseline. i also observed centroid directions shifted for a subset of Spanish queries.
maria: can you paste a quick snippet of the eval summary?
anya: eval-bot: finish summary: baseline recall@10=0.812, bn-v2 recall@10=0.753, recall@1 delta=-0.05, mean cosine shift -0.012. p95 latency +3ms.
liam: whoa recall dip is big. do we have embedding norm distributions?
anya: attaching numbers inline: baseline mean norm=0.97, std=0.12; bn-v2 mean norm=0.81, std=0.21.
sam: that increased std is suspicious. batchnorm folding maybe leaking train statistics. was running-mode preserved (eval vs train) at export?
anya: exported with eval model.eval() and fused BN->affine fold script. i can share the small export snippet: ```python
model.eval()
fold_batchnorm(model)
torch.jit.save(trace, 'bn_v2.pt')
```
liam: hmm folding script uses running_mean/var — if those weren't updated from the finetune data distribution that could bias. were running stats updated after finetune?
anya: finite-tune ran for 2k steps, but we relied on momentum defaults. i didn't do a final bn recalibration sweep.
nina: can we try post-export BN calibration: one-epoch pass of holdout shards with no labels to update running stats, then re-export? might fix centroids.
anya: willing to try. queueing a quick calib pass now, will post run id.
ops-bot: deploy triggered by anya (bn-v2-calib-pass). shard workers=8, sample=10k shards.
eval-bot: calib run finished: run_calib_6832101189. updated running stats applied.
liam: nice. re-run eval?
anya: re-eval complete: recall@10 now 0.803 (delta vs baseline -0.009), recall@1 -0.012, mean cos shift -0.002. p95 latency unchanged.
sam: much better. looks like BN running stats were the issue. we should add a mandatory post-finetune batchnorm recalibration step in the onboard checklist.
maria: Agreed. action: add single-pass calibration to model-onboard.md and CI step. i'll open a PR.
liam: also suggest adding a small sanity metric: norm distribution KL to baseline; if KL>0.05 fail.
nina: and flag language-segmented recall drops (e.g., Spanish) as a required check.
anya: created note in the run: "bn-v2: added calibration pass, re-eval passed threshold, will stage canary".
maria: PR opened -> https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/4021 : adds bn recalibration step + KL check.
anya: thanks all. leaving canary build running for 2 hours, will post any regressions. :thumbsup:
liam: thanks — great catch, quick iteration. :rocket:
